💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that his cameras had captured a series of photographs of a Canada lynx (Lynx canadensis)—a wild cat that hasn’t been documented in the state for around 25 years.
  • “It caught my eye because the cat in the image had the characteristic ear tufts and facial ruff [of bobcats], but it was lacking the black spots that are typical of bobcats,” Grooms, who is studying in the department of Fish, Wildlife and Conservation Ecology, tells Popular Science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in June, Newly introduced Mexico State University graduate student William Grooms was using motion-sensing cameras to investigate wildlife in Carson National Forest in northern New Mexico. And when he looked through his first images, he spotted something flabbergasting.

Industry observers note that his cameras had captured a series of photographs of a Canada lynx (Lynx canadensis)—a wild cat that hasn’t been documented in the state for around 25 years. But Grooms had to make sure it wasn’t actually a bobcat (Lynx rufus), which is a similar-looking species.

“It caught my eye because the cat in the image had the characteristic ear tufts and facial ruff [of bobcats], but it was lacking the black spots that are typical of bobcats,” Grooms, who is studying in the department of Fish, Wildlife and Conservation Ecology, tells Popular Science. “We also have a good image of the tail, which on lynx has a solid black tip compared to a bobcat whose tail has white on the underside, so my confidence grew.”.

He and his team also showed the image to other researchers for confirmation. Ultimately, there’s no doubt about the fact that the massive cat slinking through the dark was indeed a Canada lynx. The species lives in dense boreal and subalpine forests and woodlands throughout much of Canada and Alaska. They have long legs, grayish or yellowish-brown coats, and wide fur-lined paws.

Their main prey are snowshoe hares (Lepus americanus), which they follow into the forest understory—the ground-level area of downed trees and dense vegetation beneath which the hares hide and live. The problem is that these kinds of habitats are fire hazards. Recent forest fire mitigation efforts include decreasing dangerous fuel loads via thinning, prescribed burning, or timber harvesting.

In a recent development, “While these tactics reduce the risk of severe fires, they also remove vital habitat features,” Grooms explains. “Our objective is to provide managers with practical, science-based advice regarding what effects fuel reduction treatments and timber harvesting have on wildlife in the Southern Rocky Mountains so that they can make well-informed decisions as they go about their task of managing our nation’s forests.”.

Simply knowing that at least one Canada lynx was in the area provides more data for this mission.

Industry News: Ghosts don’t scare German shepherds

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the German shepherd was originally bred to do exactly what their name implies, but a lot has changed since Max von Stephanitz introduced the breed in 1899.
  • It has been revealed that but a good “work” German shepherd and a good show dog require two very different sets of traits.
  • “It’s interesting that we can now see that this selective breeding has indeed led to differences between working dogs and show dogs among German shepherds—differences that can be seen at both the behavioral and genetic levels,” Uppsala University genomics researcher Kerstin Lindblad-Toh explained in a recent profile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the German shepherd was originally bred to do exactly what their name implies, but a lot has changed since Max von Stephanitz introduced the breed in 1899. Today, the German shepherd is one of the world’s most recognizable and popular dogs, largely due to their intelligence, trainability, and companionship. You’re just as likely to spot one of them at an airport sniffing for contraband as you are at a kennel club competition.

It has been revealed that but a good “work” German shepherd and a good show dog require two very different sets of traits. According to researchers at Sweden’s Uppsala University, these specific qualities are so pronounced that they’re even visible at the genetic level. What’s more, many of these genes can also be seen in humans.

“It’s interesting that we can now see that this selective breeding has indeed led to differences between working dogs and show dogs among German shepherds—differences that can be seen at both the behavioral and genetic levels,” Uppsala University genomics researcher Kerstin Lindblad-Toh explained in a recent profile.

Lindblad-Toh and her colleagues laid out their findings in a study recently published in the journal Animal Genetics. To assess the iconic breed, the team reviewed a massive dataset of 23,000 German shepherds who previously participated in a standardized behavioral test known as the Dog Mentality Assessment (DMA). During the DMA, canines are exposed to a range of situations, such as meeting strangers, play time, and even encountering imposing, ghostly figures. The team discovered that while German shepherds often scored higher for traits like neuroticism and shyness, the breed’s working dogs generally exhibited more curiosity, less fear, and a willingness to socialize with people.

“Breeders of working dogs have selected and bred the ones that really enjoy working; it’s a bit like a game for them,” stated Lindblad-Toh.

According to recent reports, from there, the researchers gathered blood samples and mapped the genomes of 373 German shepherds who previously took the DMA. Some of these behavioral divergences were so stark that the study’s authors could pinpoint them in the dogs’ genetics.

In a recent development, “We could then see that there were areas in the genome where differences could be seen in the dogs depending on how curious or playful they were, for example,” Lindblad-Toh mentioned. “That meant that we were able to identify some of the genes in working dogs that are linked to curiosity and playfulness.”.

Recent findings suggest that in some instances, the same genes influencing German shepherd personalities are also tied to the same behaviors in humans. This means it may be possible to further explore human psychology with the aid of our best animal friends. Although Lindblad-Toh cautioned that their study is “just a first step” along this path, they hope to learn more about specific breed genetic traits and their overlap with owners.

“We now have an example of how we might also acquire more knowledge about different behaviors in people with [the] help of dogs in the longterm,” she said.

  • Sources indicate that the annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hospital ratings have become an important resource for choosing where to receive care. They influence which doctors patients choose, how far they are willing to travel, and whether they seek care at a different facility.

On October 27, Healthgrades revealed the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.

Sources indicate that the annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States. Healthgrades is the leading platform used by Americans for finding a doctor or hospital.

New research from Healthgrades highlights that hospital quality is increasingly a factor in healthcare decisions.

Around 80% of patients report that when looking for a doctor, the quality of the hospital where they practice matters. Additionally, 7 in 10 patients (68%) say they’re more likely to seek care for a procedure or health condition from a doctor who works at a hospital with high quality ratings.

What’s more, around 71% of patients say they would switch doctors to gain access to a higher-rated hospital.

“Our specialty awards identify the nation’s top-performing hospitals across numerous medical specialties, helping consumers find high quality care tailored to their specific needs,” remarked Alana Biggers, MD, MPH, medical advisor at Healthgrades.

Sources indicate that healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

According to recent reports, “Navigating the complex healthcare system can feel daunting, but taking a proactive stance to understand where to access superior care can enhance your healthcare journey and overall experience. The ability to make informed decisions about your health — and where to get care — is a cornerstone of self-advocacy, and we are proud to help make that information accessible to all patients.”.

Healthgrades identifies hospitals that deliver exceptional outcomes across common outpatient procedures and specialty conditions.

Finding high quality care is vital, particularly amid a growing gap between top-performing and one-star hospitals.

According to Healthgrades, from 2023 to 2025, if all hospitals had performed at the five-star level from 2023 to 2025:.

“One of the biggest challenges is balancing increasing patient needs with the resources available to healthcare professionals,” Biggers said.

“Hospitals face workforce shortages, growing administrative responsibilities, financial pressures, and increasing complexity in patient care. Physicians and other healthcare professionals need adequate time and support not only to evaluate and treat patients, but also to communicate results, coordinate follow-up care, and address concerns that arise between visits,” she continued.

“When healthcare teams are adequately supported, they are better positioned to communicate effectively with patients, coordinate care, and address patients’ needs.”.

Biggers said that ensuring equal access to quality healthcare is challenging because of factors such as:.

Sources indicate that hospital closures and reduced services make access even more difficult. Biggers identified a few possible solutions, such as expanding outpatient care, building community partnerships, using telehealth when appropriate, and improving coordination among healthcare providers.

Recent findings suggest that “Ultimately, providing high quality care requires more than clinical expertise. It requires healthcare systems to invest in their workforce, strengthen care coordination, and create environments where healthcare professionals have the resources they need to provide safe, effective, and patient-centered care,” Biggers remarked.

“Equally key, healthcare systems must ensure that patients have meaningful access to these services, regardless of where they live or their socioeconomic circumstances.”.

Healthgrades acknowledges hospitals that excel in three aspects of specialty care:.

Biggers said that outstanding hospitals recognize that high quality care extends beyond just treating an illness.

“It involves listening to patients, understanding their individual circumstances, and ensuring they feel respected, informed, and involved in their healthcare decisions,” she mentioned.

Patients want to find a hospital that excels in the procedures or health conditions relevant to them.

The recipients of the Specialty Excellence Awards are among the top 15% of hospitals specializing in these areas.

Healthgrades evaluated patient outcomes at roughly 4,500 hospitals across 31 common procedures and conditions to reach their decisions.

Among the list of Specialty Excellence Award recipients, Healthgrades also recognizes America’s 100 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for 11 specialty areas andAmerica’s 50 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for four specialty areas.

“An outstanding hospital prioritizes both patient care and the people delivering that care,” Biggers told Healthline.

Industry observers note that “While clinical outcomes, patient safety, and access to evidence-based treatments are essential measures of quality, I believe hospitals must also invest in workforce development and support. This means ensuring physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals have appropriate staffing levels, adequate clinical and administrative support, and opportunities for continued professional development,” she continued.

Healthgrades awards U.S. hospitals that excel at Outpatient Orthopedic Surgery, Outpatient Joint Replacement, andOutpatient Prostate Care.

Recent findings suggest that outpatient care is one of the fastest-growing areas of healthcare. The number of orthopedic procedures performed in an outpatient environment has grown exponentially in recent years.

From 2020 to 2025, outpatient hip replacement procedures grew by 81%, while inpatient procedures dropped by 75%. Outpatient knee replacements increased by 71% while inpatient volumes decreased by 70%.

“I believe several factors are contributing to the growing demand for outpatient care, including advances in medical technology, a greater emphasis on preventive care, and the increasing need to manage chronic medical conditions,” Biggers noted.

Sources indicate that “Many services and procedures that previously required hospitalization can now be safely performed in outpatient settings. Patients also appreciate the convenience of receiving care closer to home and avoiding unnecessary hospital stays,” she added.

To meet the increasing demand for outpatient procedures, Biggers cautioned that healthcare systems must ensure that these services are adequately staffed and supported.

“Effective communication and coordination between outpatient providers, specialists, and hospitals are essential to maintaining continuity and quality of care,” she said.

State Rankings identify the top three or five hospitals in eligible states across 19 key specialty areas.

Healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

The rankings are based on clinical performance and build on the 2027 Healthgrades Specialty Excellence Awards Methodology.

State-level specialty care rankings help consumers find outstanding local hospitals for their condition or procedure.

The analysis used Medicare inpatient data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) from 2023 to 2025, and assessed patient outcomes across 31 conditions and procedures.

These outcomes served as the foundation for determining Specialty Excellence Awards and state hospital rankings.

With consumer-facing awards and ratings influencing healthcare decisions, transparency about their methods and limitations remains essential.

Ratings can help patients ask better questions and compare options, but they should complement — not replace — clinical guidance and informed decision making.

The methodologies for each of the specialty awards can be found on the following pages:.

For more information, Healthgrades’ Specialty Excellence Patient Advocate Center provides access to the information you need to make informed decisions about your care. This resource includes an overview of how Healthgrades picks award recipients, plus a list of the top U.S. hospitals for specialty care.

It has been revealed that to be eligible for a Specialty Excellence Award, hospitals must receive a rating in the required procedures and conditions used to determine the award. Some awards are based on a single procedure, while others are based on a grouping of procedures. To learn more about Healthgrades’ ratings and awards determination process, see the 2027 Specialty Excellence Awards and Ratings Methodology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that one little bear cub in Southeastern Alaska’s Tongass National Forest is a true model of bravery. The park’s rangers have awarded the unnamed black bear (Ursus americanus) cub with the 2026 Courageous Cub award for persevering when he got himself in a little pickle this summer. The cub belongs to a forgetful mother bear named Dory, who had two cubs this season.

“This little cub of Dory’s went on a substantial adventure. He got lost, ran down the trail a half mile and approached visitors as if to ask, ‘Are you my mommy?’ Then got scared and ran off in the wrong direction,” the Tongass rangers write. “Hours later he came running back up the trail sniffing out where mama was.”.

Black bears like this family have a very keen sense of smell. It is debated just how far away they can smell, but it is at least two miles and could be up to 20. Fortunately, the cub was able to use some of that sniffing power to find both Dory and his other sibling.

The rangers at Tongass National Forest are at the moment awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

According to recent reports, tongass is the largest national forest in the United States. It covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau, and includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. This makes the creek a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, at least 39 bears feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

It has been revealed that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

According to recent reports, surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

In a recent development, after Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) said there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a new video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

Sources indicate that on Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

As we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement says it “will not operate” without the $299 plan, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

Industry observers note that so Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

In a recent development, brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

In a recent development, the memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

In a recent development, “It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

It has been revealed that yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version highlights up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

Recent findings suggest that this Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

What do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it took a few hours longer than expected, but the SS United States now rests at the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico.
  • According to recent reports, ahead of the next phase in the United States’ recycled life, divers from the RV Explorer swam to document the vessel’s location and post-scuttling condition.
  • “It was just epic,” diver Rustin Cassway told a local Philadelphia news outlet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it took a few hours longer than expected, but the SS United States now rests at the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico. The nearly 1,000-foot-long ocean liner sank off the coast of Pensacola, Florida, to a depth of about 190 feet on November 11, where it is now officially the world’s largest artificial reef. In the years ahead, biologists and conservationists will monitor the vessel’s remains as numerous marine species slowly convert the ship into their own home.

According to recent reports, ahead of the next phase in the United States’ recycled life, divers from the RV Explorer swam to document the vessel’s location and post-scuttling condition. On November 13, the team released a brief video of their successful excursion. Interestingly, the footage shows the ship is resting upright on the ocean floor despite initially sinking on its side.

“It was just epic,” diver Rustin Cassway told a local Philadelphia news outlet. “It was very cleaned up. I mean, you could see people really took their time to clean it really nicely.”.

Industry observers note that the project marks the first time ecologists will be able to monitor a shipwreck’s transformation in real-time. Researchers now initiative to conduct annual visits to the SS United States to chart not only the artificial reef’s progress, but how the ship’s materials may affect the surrounding ocean conditions.

In its heyday, the SS United States was the world’s fastest ocean liner. Larger than the RMS Titanic, she was the most powerful, advanced, and modern passenger liner when she first took to the ocean in 1952. In addition to the 1,700 passengers, 7,935 quarts of ice cream and 500 pounds of caviar were also on board. During that maiden voyage (July 3-7, 1952), she broke the transatlantic speed record held by the RMS Queen Mary by over 10 hours. The United States made the crossing from the United Kingdom to New York in three days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes at an average speed of 40.96 mph.

She was designed by naval architect William Francis Gibbs (August 24, 1886 – September 6, 1967), and was built to be converted into a troopship if the United States Navy needed during a time of war. But she never was called into military service. Instead, the United States transported immigrants and celebrities, including future President and First Lady John and Jacqueline Kennedy, actors Grace Kelly, Gary Cooper, and Marilyn Monroe, artist Salvador Dali, and musicians Duke Ellington and Irving Berlin. Walt Disney even filmed parts of the 1962 comedy Bon Voyage aboard the ship.

An engineering marvel, some of the key design features were in the rudder, radar mast, and propellers.

The rudder was designed for good maneuverability at high speeds. The Titanic’s relatively small rudder was one factor behind the ship’s collision with an iceberg and tragic sinking in 1912.

According to recent reports, the SS United States had the latest radar equipment, which allowed the crew to see the locations of  other ships and objects in the ocean despite the weather. It was among the first ocean liners to use radar, which was located at one of the highest points on the ship, so in addition to her radar “eyes,” a lookout could be stationed there to warn the captain of any danger in the ship’s path.

Considered a top-secret design, the ship had four propellers—two with four blades and two with five. According to the SS United States Conservancy, this configuration was tested and selected for its superior hydrodynamic performance. The propeller design was overseen by a pioneering Gibbs & Cox engineer named Elaine Kaplan.

According to recent reports, ocean liners became a less attractive option once air travel became quicker and less expensive. The SS United States ceased operations in 1969, and stayed in drydock in several cities before becoming the world’s largest artificial reef.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease.
  • Recent findings suggest that both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits.
  • The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease. This is according to a study published on October 21 in the Journal of Internal Medicine.

Recent findings suggest that both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits. However, the study shows an association rather than proving that drinking tea prevents cardiovascular disease.

The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.

The study followed 485,934 people ages 30–79 from the China Kadoorie Biobank for an average of 9 years.

According to recent reports, the researchers found that regular tea drinkers had an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease compared with those who did not regularly drink tea. They also observed a 37% lower risk of ischemic stroke and a 17% lower risk of heart attack.

There was no clear link for hemorrhagic stroke or pulmonary heart disease.

It has been revealed that among people who drank tea at least weekly, the lowest estimated risk was seen in those consuming approximately 6–8 cups per day. However, the findings do not establish this as a recommended daily intake.

Amit Blumfield, MD, a cardiologist with Manhattan Cardiology in NYC who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that it is key to remember this is observational data.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of drinking black and green tea on lipids and blood pressure demonstrated only modest, non-significant benefits.

The study also had limitations, including self-reported tea consumption and the possibility that other dietary and lifestyle factors influenced the results.

“Overall, tea seems to, maybe, have some cardiovascular benefits without a significant risk, so I favor tea consumption,” he said.

Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished who was not involved in the research, emphasized that the findings do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship between drinking tea and a lower risk of vascular disease.

“Tea can be a helpful addition to a heart-healthy lifestyle, but it is not a substitute for addressing individual cardiovascular risk factors,” she remarked.

The researchers also found that drinking “burning hot” tea increased the risk of vascular disease by 16%, consistent with previous research raising concerns about the consumption of very hot beverages.

“I recommend enjoying your tea’s potential benefits by letting it cool to a comfortable sipping temperature before you drink it,” noted Routhenstein.

The study examined black, green, Oolong, and other tea types.

Sources indicate that the researchers found that black tea showed a more consistent association with a lower risk of vascular disease, which is contrary to some earlier research. However, they noted that these results don’t establish black tea as superior to green tea, and they don’t mean you should switch tea types.

“Both black and green tea are great choices for your heart health, and neither is definitively better than the other,” noted Routhenstein.

“I recommend choosing whichever you enjoy and consuming it consistently, ideally without much added sugar,” Routhenstein noted.

Blumfield also noted that adding sugar or non-sugar sweeteners may change the potential health effects of drinking tea, so the findings should not automatically be extended to sweetened tea beverages.

Some older research suggests there may be additional health benefits to drinking both black and green tea. These benefits may include:.

Routhenstein remarked that tea may also support focus and alertness, improve hydration status, and potentially play a role in metabolic health.

“Enjoying tea can be a simple way to incorporate beneficial plant compounds into your day,” she added.

While drinking tea has been considered a health-promoting habit since ancient times, more research is needed to confirm its various health benefits.

As the electric counterpart to its popular T-Cross, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer remarked the ID. Cross is “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable.”.

Sadly, VW has no intends to bring the ID. Cross to the US. In early 2027, it will launch the fresh ID. Tiguan, which will replace the outgoing ID.4 SUV.

Robo-frog swims with liquid crystal muscles powered by light

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (450 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A silicone frog built by engineers at Denmark’s Aarhus University can’t swim nearly as fast as its amphibian inspiration, but it still manages to get the job done without any moving parts.
  • The team’s novel system is detailed in a study recently published in the journal Advanced Materials Technologies.
  • Industry observers note that “I could easily imagine these robots being used as toys before we see them on rescue missions,” Cecilie Ryberg, Aarhus University chemist and study co-author, stated in a profile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A silicone frog built by engineers at Denmark’s Aarhus University can’t swim nearly as fast as its amphibian inspiration, but it still manages to get the job done without any moving parts. The odd invention owes its slow-but-steady aquatic maneuvering to a set of six artificial muscles specially designed to contract when exposed to near-infrared light.

The team’s novel system is detailed in a study recently published in the journal Advanced Materials Technologies. Although similar setups may one day boost the capabilities of soft robots tasked with search and rescue or environmental monitoring, its creators are a bit more realistic about this frog-bot’s near-term uses.

Industry observers note that “I could easily imagine these robots being used as toys before we see them on rescue missions,” Cecilie Ryberg, Aarhus University chemist and study co-author, stated in a profile. “I think people would have fun playing with a frog like this using a suitable light source.”.

Each of the robot’s muscles is built using crystal elastomers. These materials are specifically manufactured to contract while they are heating, and then revert back to their original shape once cooled. In this case, Ryberg and her collaborators also added a molecule that converts near-infrared light into heat. This allows the muscles to tighten after directly exposing them to a lamp. That mentioned, the process isn’t as simple as sticking the elastomers onto their model frog and dropping it into water.

“Getting the six muscles to work together was a major challenge,” explained Brigitte Städler, a study co-author and Aarhus University chemist. “If they don’t contract in a coordinated way, the frog won’t swim forwards. It may simply spin around.”.

A lot of trial-and-error also went into concocting the elastomers themselves. In addition to contracting properly, the material needed the proper consistency to use in a 3D printer. To do this, Ryberg experimented with various molecular ingredients and molecule chain lengths to perfect the robot muscle recipe.

“In a conventional 3D printer, you typically melt a solid plastic filament. Our material is more like very thick syrup or icing that you squeeze through a piping bag when decorating a cake,” remarked Ryberg.

The final result is a light-powered soft robot that’s quite unique, but also not in any hurry. At its best pace, the frog swam a little over three inches in about two minutes. That may not get it to its destination quickly, but the proof-of-concept successfully offers a fresh way to think about robotic design, and the ways engineers can power their creations. Until then, there is always the potential for robo-frog toys.

A baby turkey with a feather duster ‘mom’ has a newly introduced BFF

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It seems straight out of a Disney movie—wild animals from two different species becoming inseparable friends.
  • In a recent development, last spring, the wildlife center received two likely orphaned turkey poults (young turkeys).
  • According to recent reports, “Since we never raise baby animals alone, we had to find a companion for the remaining poult,” the wildlife center wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems straight out of a Disney movie—wild animals from two different species becoming inseparable friends. And yet that’s what happened at the Raven Ridge Wildlife Center in southeastern Pennsylvania, between a turkey and a mourning dove.

In a recent development, last spring, the wildlife center received two likely orphaned turkey poults (young turkeys). To calm them down, the team put them with a feather-duster as a stand-in mother turkey. Because turkey poults are easily stressed, they are difficult to rehabilitate, according to a Facebook post by the wildlife center. In fact, one of them didn’t make it.

According to recent reports, “Since we never raise baby animals alone, we had to find a companion for the remaining poult,” the wildlife center wrote. “We paired it with a baby mourning dove of similar size, hoping they would comfort each other while eating and exploring as they are both ground eaters.”.

The pairing turned out to be a raging success. They formed an inseparable bond that Raven Ridge Wildlife Center had never seen before. Months later, the team gave the dove a soft release, meaning the bird could leave whenever it wanted. But he clearly had no intention of leaving his friend. The dove continued returning to the turkey’s cage, and the two would sit near each other on either side of the separation.

“After a few days, we put the dove back in with the turkey, and it was clear they were happiest together,” the wildlife center explained. But “we knew keeping them caged for the rest of their lives, or keeping them just because they were cute, was neither an option nor fair to these wild animals.”.

Recent findings suggest that as such, the team contacted a large sanctuary in Pennsylvania to request a joint release. This way, the duo could choose whether to stick together or follow their own paths. After their soft release, the dove flew into the trees and the turkey started foraging, free to stick together or join other members of their species.

“We don’t know if they’ll stay together, but our team made sure they had a safe place until they were ready to be on their own,” the wildlife center concluded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to mountain towns, there’s good, there’s great, and then there’s Aspen—so needless to say, Aspen’s hotels are the height of luxury. Among one of the world’s finest ski towns (with a whopping four mountains on one lift ticket), this winter wonderland is rife with dazzling accommodations. The best hotels in Aspen offer everything: luxury spa experiences; fine dining; ski-in, ski-out access; and all the après-ski cocktails you can get your hands on.

Industry observers note that if resort life isn’t quite your speed, fear not—there are plenty of picture-perfect rentals you can snag on Airbnb or Vrbo. Expect a robust selection of spacious condominiums, luxury mountain chalets, and backcountry cabins, most of which are within walking distance from one of Snowmass or Aspen Mountain’s peak-reaching gondolas and ski resorts.

Industry observers note that don’t love the snow? Good thing Aspen is a top-tier year-round destination. Ideal for climbers, equestrians, cyclists, and other adventure-seekers, the Rocky Mountains provide a backdrop for just about any summertime alpine experience you can dream up. The town’s famed Food & Wine Classic in June is also a can’t miss. Each luxury hotel and off-the-beaten-path rental we found offers access to some of the best adventures in the West, whether you visit in January, July, or anytime in between. Consider this your cue to scroll below and book your stay while date availability lasts.

Perks: Daily champagne sabering, full-service spa, heated outdoor pool, multiple on-site restaurants, pet-friendly, valet parking.

In a recent development, for the ultimate choice in old-school luxury, check in to the St. Regis. The grand, chalet-style property sits at the foot of Aspen Mountain—just a five-minute walk from the Silver Queen Gondola—and pairs classic Rocky Mountain charm with five-star hospitality. Inside, rooms are outfitted with buttery leather headboards, fine linens, marble bathrooms, and mountain views framed by mahogany trim, while the hotel’s on-call butler service can handle tasks like unpacking luggage and drawing a post-ski bath. The RAKxa Wellness Spa remains one of the best in town, offering oxygen facials, a heated outdoor pool (perfect for a post-slopes soak), and many more wellness-minded amenities. Still, this grande dame doesn’t take itself too seriously. Since 2023, it’s been home to The Snow Lodge, a winter spinoff of Montauk’s famed Surf Lodge. The après scene here has become the hottest ticket in Aspen—Diplo, Rampa, and Bob Moses have all spun sets in the open-air courtyard—while the group’s newly introduced supper club and nightlife concept brings coastal-cool energy to the Rockies with candlelit dinners, Champagne towers, and late-night dancing under the stars. It’s a rare blend of heritage and hedonism—the kind of place where you can trade ski boots for stilettos without missing a beat. From $649 per night.

Perks: Fitness center, multiple restaurants and bars, in-town transport, heated pool and hot tubs, pet-friendly.

Perks: Ski-in/ski-out, heated outdoor pool, spa and fitness center, airport transfers, concierge desk, complimentary mini bar snacks and soft drinks.

Recent findings suggest that the only AAA Five Diamond–rated hotel in Aspen, the Little Nell blends the best of the West with the cosmopolitan luxuries you’d expect from a five-star hotel. Every detail is dialed in. Guests can unwind at the heated outdoor pool and hot tub, book a treatment at the Little Nell Spa, or rely on the property’s Les Clefs d’Or–certified concierge team, who have a reputation for making the impossible happen (heli-skiing trip to Telluride, anyone?). Food and wine take center stage here, too—the hotel’s Chefs & Somms dinners pair Michelin-caliber cuisine with rare vintages from a 20,000-bottle cellar, one of the most impressive in the Rockies. But it’s on the mountain where The Little Nell truly shines. The Ski Concierge team can arrange first tracks before the lifts open, snowcat powder tours, or private gear fittings in your room, ensuring you’re perfectly prepped with your helmet and bindings. From $800 per night.

Perks: Rooftop hot tub, lobby bar and restaurant, pet-friendly, EV charging.

Sources indicate that for a quieter boutique experience, you’ll want to stay at Mollie Aspen. Opened in late 2023, the hotel blends Japanese and Scandinavian design, creating an atmosphere that feels immediately restorative. Roomy plush leather chairs, well-worn rugs, custom woodwork, and a plethora of unique design accents welcome weary travelers and exhausted skiers, exuding the type of vibe you’d expect from a well-loved and hard-to-reach mountain chalet. Despite the tucked-away vibe, Mollie’s location couldn’t be more central—you’re steps from downtown’s galleries, the Aspen Art Museum, and cultural landmarks like the Aspen Institute and Wheeler Opera House. If you’re too tired for a jaunt downtown, the Mollie also has a lobby restaurant and poolside rooftop bar where you can while away the hours. The rooftop, in particular, has become a gathering spot for the design-savvy après crowd, offering mountain views and mellow vinyl playlists. From $278 per night.

Perks: All-suite accommodations, outdoor heated lap pool and hot tub, fitness center, tennis and pickleball courts, shuttle service.

Backed up against the Rocky Mountains, Aspen Meadows Resort is a midcentury masterpiece tailor-made for design aficionados. Originally conceived as part of the Aspen Institute campus by artist and architect Herbert Bayer, the property is steeped in Bauhaus principles, with clean lines, geometric forms, and a playful use of primary colors throughout its public and private spaces. Best for art and design nerds, the resort’s 98 suites feature Bauhaus-inspired furnishings, while common spaces include art exhibitions, outdoor sculptures, and West End Social, a recently redesigned restaurant with aspen-wood paneling, Colorado marble, and colorful textiles. Some of the stand-out amenities include a shuttle service with routes into town and the Aspen airport, a heated saline pool and hot tub, and ski butler service. When you’re looking to venture outside of the hotel’s chic walls, there are 40 acres to explore, which include plenty of great sledding hills for those visiting in the winter months and a massive sculpture collection. There’s also the on-site Resnick Center for Herbert Bayer Studies, where rotation exhibitions explore the artist’s legacy. With so much space for playing, there are more activities for visitors than could fit into 10 different trips. Can’t-miss itinerary items include themed scavenger hunts, hot-air balloon rides, fly fishing, snowshoeing, and—of course—lots of skiing. From $359 per night.

Perks: Airport shuttle, pet-friendly, on-site fitness room, rooftop lounge.

In a recent development, for travelers who want to be right in the heart of it all, The Limelight Hotel Aspen offers front-row access to the town’s best shops, restaurants, and bars—plus it’s just steps from the Silver Queen Gondola, which whisks skiers to the top of Aspen Mountain in under 20 minutes. The atmosphere is lively yet low-key, thanks to communal spaces like the buzzy lounge, where locals and visitors gather for wood-fired pizzas, live music, and craft cocktails. The property staff helps guests craft the perfect stay, with activities including hiking adventures, whitewater rafting, art museum visits, and more. Some rooms feature balconies and patios and are draped in mountain charm (think: wool blankets and fireplaces). From $299 per night.

Perks: Mountain view, wood-burning fireplace, fully equipped kitchen, in-unit laundry, hot tub, security system, free parking, housekeeping available for a fee.

Just a block from the Silver Queen Gondola, this newly renovated two-bedroom condo makes it easy to spend mornings skiing Aspen Mountain and afternoons exploring the restaurants, boutiques, and après-ski spots in Aspen’s downtown area. Inside, cozy furnishings and a wood-burning fireplace make the living room an inviting place to warm up after a day on the slopes. The two bedrooms offer flexible sleeping arrangements, with a king bed in the primary suite and two twins that can be converted into another king in the second bedroom. The kitchen is outfitted with stainless steel appliances, an induction cooktop, and all the cooking equipment needed to whip up dinner at home, though with Ajax Tavern so close, you might not bother. From $865 per night.

Perks: Heated outdoor pool, fully equipped kitchen, in-unit laundry, pet-friendly, free parking.

Sources indicate that there is a lot of architectural woodwork to behold in this modern Aspen condo, but thanks to an abundance of windows, the effect reads bright and airy rather than moody ski lodge. Paneled ceilings, exposed timber rafters, wood floors, and floor-to-ceiling cabinetry bring plenty of warmth to the interiors, while clean-lined furnishings give the two-bedroom space a more contemporary feel. Equipped with one king bedroom and one queen, the condo is particularly well suited to two couples traveling together or a family of four. In the exteriors, the heated pool offers another way to unwind, though the slopes are hardly far away: The property sits just off the Lower Corkscrew run on Aspen Mountain, steps from Lift 1A. From $1,272 per night.

Perks: Mountain views, private patio, soaking tub, in-unit laundry, free parking, pet-friendly, housekeeping available for a fee.

In a recent development, aspen's Victorian-era architecture is every bit as charming as its mountain scenery, and this one-bedroom apartment near Pioneer Park puts you in the middle of one of the town's most scenic historic neighborhoods. Recently remodeled, the 540-square-foot space has bright, sunlight interiors that includes an open-strategy kitchen and living room that seems considerably larger thanks to oversized windows lining the walls. A queen bedroom separates guests from the main living area, and modern conveniences like air-conditioning, a dishwasher, and in-unit laundry make longer stays especially comfortable. Although the apartment sits on a peaceful residential street, downtown Aspen's restaurants, boutiques, and the historic Wheeler Opera House are just a short walk away, and a nearby bus stop makes getting to the ski slopes easy. From $391 per night.

Perks: Wrap-around deck, washer and dryer, wood burning fireplace, Wi-fi.

Recent findings suggest that tucked just behind the St. Regis, this one-bedroom apartment puts you right in the center of Aspen without feeling caught in the crowd. The interiors are warm and functional rather than flashy—a wood-burning fireplace, buttery cotton linens from Garnier-Thiebaut, and plenty of closet space for your suitcases give the space an easy, lived-in comfort. A wraparound deck nearly doubles the footprint, inviting morning coffee in the sun or an après-ski glass of wine with views of the surrounding peaks. Everything is set up to make a stay feel effortless. There’s dedicated parking, air conditioning, and in-unit laundry, plus a Sonos sound system and high-speed Wi-Fi for streaming or working remotely. The open kitchen has all the essentials, while the living room feels like a natural place to gather after a day outside. Professionally managed by Aspen Vacations, guests enjoy thoughtful extras—an invitation to the members-only Caribou Club, and insider tips on local dining and trail access are just a couple to name. Steps from world-class restaurants, boutiques, and the Silver Queen Gondola, this retreat feels equal parts modern pied-à-terre and alpine hideaway—a polished perch for soaking in the best of Aspen, no ski-valet required. From $408 per night.

Perks: Fireplace, free parking, washer and dryer, shared pool and hot tub.

According to recent reports, right on the edge of downtown Aspen, this riverfront condo feels worlds away from the bustle. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame the Roaring Fork River, filling the space with natural light and the sound of rushing water. Inside, the palette is crisp and minimal—soft grays, creamy whites, and natural wood—letting the view take center stage. The open living area flows onto a private balcony, and a sleek kitchen with stainless appliances and stone counters may convince you to eat in. Better yet, there’s some practical touches, like in-unit laundry and high-speed internet, as well as amenities more commonly seen in hotels, such as a shared indoor pool, hot tub, and gym. From $412 per night.

Craving an escape? From colorful carry-ons to cleverly designed packing cubes (how did we ever travel without them?), shop everything you need to make the journey in style—and as streamlined and stress-free as possible.

Drug-Resistant ‘Superbugs’ Linked to More Than 50,000 Deaths a Year, CDC Claims

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.
  • In a recent development, the updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year.
  • The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.

In a recent development, the updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year. This is up from 2.8 million in a similar report from 2019.

The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.

Industry observers note that the latest report also noted that infections that commonly occur in people in the hospital account for more than 42,000 deaths and cost the U.S. healthcare system more than $12 billion.

According to recent reports, these findings are based on 2023 data. Officials from the CDC stated that the increase in drug-resistant infections from 2019 partially reflects a real rise in infections caused by certain resistant bacteria and fungi. However, they also noted that data sources and methodologies have changed, and direct comparisons between the two reports shouldn’t be made.

“These numbers are alarming by any measure but are particularly sobering when infectious diseases physicians connect real patients with these statistics in their everyday experience,” Wendy Armstrong, MD, President of the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), mentioned in a statement.

Industry observers note that the CDC report highlighted 19 drug-resistant pathogens responsible for the 9.7 million annual infections. Four of these pathogens are classified as urgent threats, 13 as serious threats, and 2 as concerning.

The CDC also maintains a watch list that presently includes six pathogens.

The four pathogens classified as urgent threats are:.

William Schaffner, MD, a professor of the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, told Healthline that the reason for this increase in superbugs is, “Overuse of antibiotics; using them for too long or in circumstances where they do not offer a benefit.”.

In a recent development, “An example of the latter is the antibiotic treatment of common viral respiratory infections — antibiotics have no effect on viral infections. The widespread use of antibiotics kills off those bacteria that are susceptible to antibiotics, but then can leave a few bacterial survivors that are resistant to the effect of the antibiotics, resulting in the spread of these resistant strains,” he noted.

Monica Gandhi, MD, a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, agreed and added, “This widespread use leads to selective drug pressure on the pathogen to evolve resistance to these antibiotics, making them harder to treat.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The risk to public health from these bugs is substantial. In fact, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates up to 5 million deaths from these bugs worldwide every year, making these a substantial public health threat,” remarked Gandhi.

Candida auris tops the list of urgent threats.

Recent findings suggest that cases have increased nearly tenfold since the first detection in hospitals 10 years ago. This includes a more than 50% jump between 2022 and 2023.

It has been revealed that candida auris is a fungus that is almost completely resistant to one class of antifungal medications. It has also shown emerging resistance to the other two classes.

This fungus is often found on people’s skin, spreads rapidly in healthcare settings like hospitals, and affects some of the most vulnerable individuals.

It has been revealed that CRE is a family of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens. They have become increasingly difficult to treat and can share resistance with other bacteria.

These bacteria also pose a significant threat to people in hospitals, especially those with devices such as ventilators and catheters. A recent study found that CRE cases at U.S. hospitals increased by 18% between 2019 and 2023.

Industry observers note that while those in hospitals are especially vulnerable to CRE, 67% of the cases in 2023 were in the community. However, some of these cases may have occurred in people with recent exposure to healthcare.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the bacterium that causes gonorrhea, which is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections.

The CDC report noted that only a few antibiotics can effectively treat this infection.

Without effective treatment, gonorrhea can lead to:.

There are ways you can help prevent these superbugs:.

“[One] way individuals can help prevent the evolution of these superbugs is to not ask for antibiotics from their providers or urgent care settings in the setting of a viral infection,” said Gandhi.

Experts and organizations like the CDC are working together to find ways to reduce the spread of these superbugs.

“Professional organizations and hospitals are educating their doctors and staff about the antibiotic resistance problem and have created reviews of practice patterns to encourage the appropriate use of antibiotics,” mentioned Schaffner.

Gandhi added that organizations should institute procedures, such as “antimicrobial stewardship programs,” to ensure that providers do not prescribe antibiotics for non-bacterial infections and narrow antibiotics as soon as possible.

The Pioneering Antimicrobial Subscriptions to End Upsurging Resistance (PASTEUR) Act aims to revitalize antibiotic and antifungal development by changing the way the federal government pays for novel antimicrobials.

This act was reintroduced in Congress in February and is presently under review.

The focus on reducing the spread of superbugs and developing latest antibiotics is notable.

Recent findings suggest that “You really cannot have all the benefits of modern medicine, even outside the realm of infectious diseases, without effective antibiotics. It all goes away,” Haley Ann Pritchard, MD, medical director of infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship at Eskenazi Health Hospital, said in a statement.

#18184. Tech Report: Muscle Size vs. Strength: Which Matters More for Living Longer? Experts Explain

Tech Report: Muscle Size vs. Strength: Which Matters More for Living Longer? Experts Explain

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that when it comes to aging well, you've probably heard that building muscle is one of the best things you can do for your body.
  • According to recent reports, resistance training, which is often used as an umbrella term, can have different goals, including building muscle size and increasing maximal strength.
  • On the other hand, training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force your muscles can produce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that when it comes to aging well, you've probably heard that building muscle is one of the best things you can do for your body. And it's true: Maintaining muscle mass is essential for staying healthy, mobile, and independent as you get older. But here's something you might not realize: Having more muscle doesn't necessarily mean you're stronger. And when it comes to living as long (and as well!) as possible, that distinction matters.

According to recent reports, resistance training, which is often used as an umbrella term, can have different goals, including building muscle size and increasing maximal strength. Training for muscle growth, known as hypertrophy training, focuses on increasing the size of your muscles, notes Vonda Wright, MD, an orthopedic surgeon who researches longevity and muscle health.

On the other hand, training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force your muscles can produce. It’s often measured by how much weight you can lift in a particular exercise, Dr. Wright explains. Although larger muscles have the potential to produce more force, muscle size alone doesn’t determine strength. “That’s why someone who is smaller can sometimes be stronger than someone with visibly larger muscles,” she adds.

Meet the experts: Vonda Wright, MD, is an orthopedic surgeon and author of Unbreakable. Mark Kovacs, PhD, CSCS, is an exercise physiologist, longevity and human performance specialist, and founder of the Kovacs Institute in Atlanta. Stuart Phillips, PhD, is a muscle researcher and professor of kinesiology at McMaster University. Ben Walker, CPT, is a personal trainer and founder of Anywhere Fitness in Dublin, Ireland.

According to recent reports, still, both adaptations play an key role in healthy aging—especially since muscle mass and strength naturally decline with age. Building muscle supports your joints and bones, helps regulate metabolic health, and gives you the strength and physical capacity to keep moving and stay active, states Mark Kovacs, PhD, CSCS, an exercise physiologist, longevity and human performance specialist, and founder of the Kovacs Institute. Strength, meanwhile, allows you to put that muscle to work, whether you’re carrying groceries, climbing stairs, or getting up from the floor, he explains.

It’s imperative to build both strength and muscle for a long, healthy life. But if your goal is to stay active and independent well into your later years, one may be worth prioritizing over the other.

According to recent reports, resistance training can help you build muscle and become stronger, but these are distinct goals that emphasize different outcomes. Training for muscle growth focuses on increasing muscle size, while training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force you can produce, says Kovacs. The two goals overlap, and people typically gain both muscle and strength through resistance training. But you can formulate your workouts to emphasize one outcome over the other, he adds.

It has been revealed that for instance, if your goal is maximal strength, the weight you lift matters more. So, training for strength means practicing movements with loads that feel heavy to you, says Stuart Phillips, PhD, a muscle researcher and professor of kinesiology at McMaster University. Strength gains depend not only on muscle size, but also on how effectively your nervous system activates your muscles and how efficiently you perform the movement. “Lighter weights can still make you stronger, but taking them to failure doesn’t automatically make them equivalent to heavier training for maximizing strength,” Phillips explains. For this goal, he recommends 2 to 3 sets of roughly 4 to 8 reps with a challenging weight, stopping before your technique breaks down.

Industry observers note that in terms of muscle growth, both lighter and heavier weights can build muscle—what matters is that your body is sufficiently challenged. Of course, lighter weights will require more repetitions to grow muscle, Phillips notes. (In fact, his research indicates that performing roughly 20 to 25 repetitions with light weights produced similar muscle growth to sets of 8 to 12 repetitions with heavier weights when both were taken to failure.).

Sources indicate that as a rule of thumb, Phillips recommends choosing a weight that makes the last few reps feel challenging while leaving about two good reps in reserve. (If you finish 25 reps and feel like you could easily do five more, the weight is probably too light to provide enough of a stimulus to spark growth.) One way to gauge this is with the resistance-training rating of perceived exertion (RPE) scale, which measures how hard a set feels based on how many more reps you think you could complete with good form, he explains. The scale runs from 1 to 10: An RPE of eight means you could squeeze out about two more reps, a 9 means you have one left, and a 10 means you’ve reached failure and can’t complete another rep.

The number of sets you perform matters for building muscle, too. Doing one challenging set per exercise consistently over time can grow muscle, Phillips says, but research suggests that performing multiple sets generally leads to greater muscle growth.

Recent findings suggest that strength, which is the maximum force you can produce in a particular task, directly influences how well you can move through everyday life. “Strong muscles support our skeleton, protect our joints, improve metabolic health, and allow us to continue doing the things we love at 50, 70, and 90,” says Dr. Wright. Strength helps us with getting up off the floor, carrying our own suitcase, climbing a mountain, playing with grandchildren, and living independently long-term.

Consider something as simple as getting out of a chair. When you’re younger and stronger, Kovacs notes that movement may require only a small percentage of your maximum strength. As you lose strength with age, though, that same movement requires more of what you have available. If you aren’t regularly training it, everyday activities can become increasingly difficult, he explains. But when you continue to build strength as you age, you have more to pull from, making those activities easier.

Additionally, research draws a direct connection between strength and a longer life: A 2026 study in JAMA Network Open looked at the association between muscular strength and mortality. Over 5,000 women ages 63 to 99 underwent testing for grip strength, chair stand performance, and a timed walk test. Participants also mailed health update questionnaires annually between 2012 and 2014 until 2023. They found that higher muscle strength was associated with lower mortality.

Strength training is also associated with cardiometabolic benefits, endurance performance, and bone density—which are all vital for living long and well. In fact, a small 2022 study in Sensors had 29 postmenopausal women with osteopenia or osteoporosis (when you have lower bone mineral density than normal) either do strength training exercises with heavy and moderately heavy weights, or no exercise at all, for six months. The group that strength trained had higher bone mineral density at the end of the trial period.

Muscle is one of your body’s best forms of insurance for getting older. Everyday activities depend on having enough muscle (as well as strength) to do them independently. “Muscle supports our joints and loads our bones, helping stimulate the bone-building process, but it’s also essential to mobility and functional strength," Dr. Wright explains. “If we want to continue getting ourselves off the ground, climbing stairs, carrying things, traveling, playing sports, and living independently, we need muscle to do it.”.

Research also concludes that less muscle mass is associated with a higher risk of mortality. A 2023 review in PLOS One observed 16 studies with over 81,000 participants and looked at the connection between their body composition and when they died. The review concluded that a low skeletal muscle mass index was significantly associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality.

Additionally, having muscle mass can improve your metabolic health. A 2025 study in Nutrition & Metabolism had older participants with type 2 diabetes either build muscle through resistance training alone, resistance training and eating a whey protein supplement, or doing neither of the two, for 12 weeks. Those who completed the muscle-building interventions significantly improved their blood glucose control and insulin resistance.

It has been revealed that plus, lower muscle mass is linked to poor balance and a higher risk of falls. So, maintaining muscle helps protect your mobility and independence as you age, Dr. Wright adds. A 2020 study in Menopause Review had 122 women over 60 do physical performance tests (gait speed test, grip strength, and a timed up and go). Their body composition was measured, and they filled out a survey of how often they fell in the past year. Less muscle was associated with a higher risk of falls.

A well-rounded workout blueprint should naturally progress both muscular size and strength. After all, they address different pieces of the same puzzle and one form of training can help you make progress in the other. As you build muscle, you generally increase the amount of tissue available to produce force, states Ben Walker, CPT, a certified personal trainer and founder of Anywhere Fitness in Dublin, Ireland. And as you train for strength, your brain and nervous system become better at coordinating and activating those muscles, he explains.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a plan that’ll help you build both strength and muscle, check out our Women’s Health+ exclusive workout aims. Each one comes with four weeks of expert-programmed workouts, science-backed nutrition advice, and evidence-based recovery methods.

It has been revealed that remember, longevity isn’t about simply adding years to your life. It’s about extending your healthspan, or the number of years you remain healthy, mobile, and strong. “The goal is to bring our healthspan as close to our lifespan as possible, and for me, that means building a body that can carry you through the life you want to live,” says Dr. Wright. That way, you’ll be ready to throw grandkids around at 60, deadlift hundreds of pounds at 70, and lift your own suitcase on vacation with your family in your 80s and beyond.

As a former collegiate pole vaulter, she loves all things fitness and has yet to meet a group workout class she doesn't like.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took a while, but Apple has finally introduced its first foldable: the iPhone Duo is now available in Star White or Night Sky finishes, starting at $1,999 and up, depending on how much storage you want inside.

In a recent development, apple has built a variety of adaptations into iOS to support the iPhone Duo, so icons and menus will shift if the software detects it’s running on the inner or outer display of the foldable, rather than a standard iPhone. In addition, iOS developers are updating their own apps to better suit the two new screen sizes introduced by the foldable.

We’re also seeing several apps built or optimized specifically for the iPhone Duo, to take advantage of that foldable screen. Whether you’ve got the phone or not, they’re worth checking out as a showcase of what’s possible with the latest form factor.

In a recent development, toastie ($2.99) is a rather whimsical game for the iPad, iPhone, and iPhone Duo. The aim is to make the best grilled sandwich you can, and on Apple’s foldable phone you snap the handset shut and open it again to control the cooking time for your toasties.

You can pick different ingredients and bread types as you go, and the ability to partially open the iPhone Duo to peek at your culinary creation is a nice touch. It’s not the most sophisticated cooking sim, but you might be surprised by how much fun it is to play.

Bring some old-school to your iPhone Duo with Tiny Computers ($3.99): With the foldable half open and propped up, the flat half turns into a virtual keyboard, and the vertical half indicates a simulated display from a classic computer of your choice—with 10 to pick from.

The available computers include vintage Windows and Mac machines, plus the Commodore 64; while these aren’t full-scale emulators, you can play around with them and discover some “nostalgic secrets” as you go (including some iconic keyboard sounds).

There are also gaming experiences specifically for the iPhone Duo to enjoy. Marbles Unhinged (freemium, $2.99 to unlock all levels) is a marble-rolling game that uses your phone’s accelerometer and gyroscope to create realistic physical tilting controls.

With the iPhone Duo half open, one half of the main display becomes the marble maze, and the other half becomes a ramp you use to get the marble moving to the right place at the right speed. There are 10 levels available to play for free before you have to pay.

Simply put, Foldissimo (free, $9.99 to unlock all the songs) turns your iPhone Duo into a virtual accordion. You can adjust the airflow affecting the instrument by folding and unfolding the Apple device—faster folds pump in more air and increase the volume.

There is a selection of classic song tutorials included to get you started, and you can compose your own too. You can also switch to other instruments, including panpipes and a theremin, but that’ll cost you extra. A clever idea, neatly implemented.

If you’ve got a hankering for the days when we carried camcorders around as separate gadgets—rather than just using our phones to record video—then Flipcorder ($4.99) is a perfect iPhone Duo app, complete with a retro-looking interface and workflow.

You can only record videos in 20-second bursts, up to 30 minutes a day, reflecting the limitations of camcorders of yesteryear. When you close the foldable, the outer display indicates your subjects what’s being filmed, which is a smart touch. (And don’t forget to back your videos up.).

Sources indicate that if you remember the Walkman era, then you’ll love Deck-Man ($4.99), which gives the iPhone Duo the feel of a classic cassette player. It interfaces with Apple Music and any music files you’ve got stored locally on your device to give audio playback a retro feel.

Your albums show up as cassette tapes, and there are chunky virtual buttons for starting and stopping the audio—with the familiar fast forward, rewind, and eject buttons here too. The app even includes authentic mechanical sounds, recorded from a real cassette player.

According to recent reports, unfold Your City (free; $4.99 to unlock all the cities) utilizes the iPhone Duo’s foldable form factor to turn the handset into a virtual pop-up book that serves as your guide to the world’s most famous cities. You can even switch between day and night modes.

It’s a fresh twist on the usual travel guide format, and plenty of care and attention has been put into the details here (nice touches include a Tower Bridge that actually opens in London). Be warned, though: the app may have a serious impact on your travel budget.
