Breaking: Plant-Based Milk Alternatives May Not Give You Enough Iodine. Here’s Why That Matters

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives (PBAs), even partially, could substantially lower iodine intake, especially if those alternatives aren’t fortified, according to a recent study published in the Lancet Planetary Health.
  • It has been revealed that the United Kingdom-based researchers found that only 12% of UK plant-based milk, yogurt, and cheese products analyzed were fortified with iodine.
  • In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provides guidance on the nutritional content of PBAs, but fortification with iodine is voluntary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives (PBAs), even partially, could substantially lower iodine intake, especially if those alternatives aren’t fortified, according to a recent study published in the Lancet Planetary Health.

It has been revealed that the United Kingdom-based researchers found that only 12% of UK plant-based milk, yogurt, and cheese products analyzed were fortified with iodine. This compares with 61% for calcium and 46% for vitamin B12.

In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provides guidance on the nutritional content of PBAs, but fortification with iodine is voluntary.

The study found that replacing as little as 20% of dairy intake with plant-based alternatives could increase the risk of inadequate iodine intake, particularly among adolescent girls and women of reproductive age.

“People often worry about a decline in calcium intake when they replace some of their dairy with plant-based alternatives. As a result, iodine is frequently overlooked. This study serves as a valuable reminder of iodine’s significance as a nutrient,” said Victoria Finn, MD, board certified endocrinologist at Medical Offices of Manhattan, who wasn’t involved in the study.

The study included analysis of UK plant-based milk, cheese, and yogurt products, as well as dietary data from 3,500 people.

The researchers used statistical modeling to predict how swapping dairy for PBAs might affect iodine and other nutrients.

The people who are most vulnerable to iodine inadequacy are adolescent females and people at reproductive age, especially those who are pregnant or who plan to become pregnant.

The researchers estimated that replacing 20% to 35% of dairy intake with PBAs would increase the proportion of people with inadequate iodine intake:.

When the researchers modeled the replacement of all dairy products with PBAs, the proportion of adolescent females with inadequate iodine intake rose to 80%. Among females ages 19 to 49, that proportion remained relatively stable as replacement rates increased.

It is vital to keep in mind that the study used dietary modeling rather than direct measurement of iodine status.

Iodine is notable for thyroid hormone production, metabolism, and both fetal and child brain development.

“Your thyroid gland requires iodine to produce thyroid hormones, which play a crucial role in regulating metabolism and supporting normal growth and development,” said Finn.

Sources indicate that she added that if you consistently consume too little iodine over an extended period, the thyroid gland may enlarge and eventually struggle to produce enough hormones. This condition is known as hypothyroidism, which can lead to various symptoms such as lethargy, sleepiness, weight gain, dry skin, and more.

“Hypothyroidism can be particularly dangerous during pregnancy, as the baby’s brain, nervous system, and organs rely heavily on the mother’s thyroid hormone during the early stages of development,” Finn added.

In the United Kingdom, dairy is a major iodine source due to cattle feed supplementation, not because dairy is naturally high in iodine.

In the United States, dairy is also an important source of iodine for the same reasons.

It has been revealed that however, the risk profile for iodine deficiency in the U.S. may differ from the U.K., as iodized salt is also a significant source of iodine and is widely available in the U.S., but not in the U.K.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the recommended daily intake of iodine depends on your age.

Sources indicate that plant-based or plant-forward diets have grown in popularity, in part due to the health benefits they offer. For example, consuming less meat can reduce your risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol.

Recent findings suggest that however, as this study suggests, it may be possible to reduce your iodine intake when transitioning to a plant-based diet. There are ways you can protect your iodine intake when choosing a more plant-forward diet, though.

Check the labels on plant-based dairy alternatives to find those fortified with iodine. You can also read the nutrition label. Iodine may be listed as potassium iodide or potassium iodate.

Seafood, eggs, and iodized salt are all good sources of iodine.

You can also discuss iodine supplements with your healthcare professional.

In a recent development, “Iodine supplements should be taken with caution, especially without checking your thyroid levels,” said Finn. “Additionally, be cautious with kelp supplements, as their iodine content can vary, and excessive iodine intake can disrupt thyroid function.”.

#18024. The Harm of Trying to Change Your Sexual Orientation

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1035 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

The Harm of Trying to Change Your Sexual Orientation

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.
  • Industry observers note that when people hear “conversion therapy,” they may picture a teenager forced into treatment by parents or religious leaders.
  • Sources indicate that in March 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that a Colorado ban on conversion therapy may violate free speech rules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

Industry observers note that when people hear “conversion therapy,” they may picture a teenager forced into treatment by parents or religious leaders. But efforts to change sexual orientation often begin privately: someone prays for their attractions to disappear, suppresses sexual thoughts, or avoids relationships in hopes of becoming heterosexual.

Sources indicate that in March 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that a Colorado ban on conversion therapy may violate free speech rules. Proponents of the ban argued that people who want to change their sexual orientation should be allowed to try. This raises an key question, answered by recent research—what happens when a person sincerely wants this change?

A fresh study offers a troubling answer: self-initiated efforts to change sexual orientation were associated with greater depression, less social support, and greater disconnection from oneself—without evidence that they changed sexual orientation. Choosing to pursue change does not establish that the pursuit is safe or effective.

Psychologist G. Tyler Lefevor and colleagues followed current and former members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints over two years. Their study included 315 participants with information about change efforts at both assessments. Unlike research that asks people to reconstruct experiences years later, this study followed participants forward in time. The researchers also registered their research initiative in advance and assembled a team with differing perspectives on sexual orientation change efforts. This is an important way the researchers demonstrated commitment to objectivity and research ethics.

In a recent development, nearly three-quarters of participants reported trying to change their same-gender sexuality at some point. Forty-three reported ongoing or recently ended efforts at the beginning of the study.

Industry observers note that those participants were struggling more than people who were no longer trying or had never tried. They reported more depressive symptoms, lower well-being, poorer self-rated health, and less support from friends and family. They were also less open about their sexuality and more alienated from their own experiences.

Two years later, the group initially pursuing change still reported more depression and less support from friends. However, the overall test combining health outcomes was not statistically significant, and the researchers found no significant difference in suicidality. The depression difference averaged about two points on a commonly used questionnaire, with both groups’ averages falling within the mild range.

These findings deserve attention. This was an observational study, and participants were already experiencing distress when it began. It cannot establish whether change efforts caused depression, whether distress encouraged people to pursue change, or whether both reflected other pressures. Most participants were White adults from one religious background, and relatively few were actively pursuing change.

Nevertheless, the findings challenge the reassurance that personally desired change efforts are harmless and should be allowed.

Recent findings suggest that A person can sincerely choose something while carrying painful beliefs about what makes them acceptable. “I want to become straight” may coexist with “I am afraid I will lose my family,” “I cannot imagine belonging in my faith community as I am,” or “My attractions mean there is something wrong with me.”.

This study did not establish that these change efforts were entirely free of outside influence. “Self-initiated” describes who undertakes the effort; it does not establish where the desire originated. Nor did it mean everyone worked alone: participants’ experiences could include personal practices, groups, or other assistance.

According to recent reports, that distinction matters. An external demand can become an internal rule, enforced without anyone else in the room.

Recent findings suggest that one possible cost is persistent self-surveillance. Every attraction or sexual thought becomes something to monitor. Every unwanted erotic desire or impulse becomes evidence of failure. When attractions persist, a person may conclude that they have not prayed enough, worked hard enough, or shown sufficient commitment.

Industry observers note that another possible cost is isolation. Avoiding people who evoke attraction—or communities that offer acceptance—may reduce opportunities for friendship, intimacy, and honest conversation. The study’s findings of lower support and greater self-alienation fit these concerns, although they do not prove these particular pathways caused the distress.

Recent findings suggest that the promised benefit also failed to materialize in the study’s comparisons. Participants pursuing change highlighted no significantly different changes in same-gender or other-gender attraction, sexual aversion, or sexual behavior over two years. Nearly 63 percent of those initially classified as pursuing change were no longer doing so by follow-up, having given up trying to change their sexuality.

Sexuality can show natural variation over time. People can also change their behavior, relationships, or identity labels. None of those changes, by itself, demonstrates that an intervention can reliably turn same-gender attraction into heterosexuality.

Respecting personal autonomy remains essential. People deserve to make their own decisions about faith, relationships, sexual behavior, and the language they use for themselves. A therapist should not prescribe a particular identity or relationship.

According to recent reports, but respecting someone’s choices also requires being honest about the evidence and helping them examine the costs of their goals. Someone seeking help can explore religious commitments, relationship decisions, grief, and fear without being promised that their attractions can be eliminated. Choosing celibacy or setting boundaries around behavior is a different goal from trying to change the attractions themselves. Sex therapist Jack Morin famously described that when people go to war with their own sexuality, they are likely to end up worse than they started.

The clinical task is to help people build a life they can inhabit with dignity, connection, and less self-rejection.

A sincere desire to become heterosexual does not guarantee that pursuing that goal will help. This research adds to concerns that the pursuit can accompany continuing distress while delivering no demonstrated change in orientation. People experiencing that conflict deserve support that takes both their values and their well-being seriously.

Source: Lefevor, G. T., Rosik, C. H., Beckstead, A. L., Mansfield, T. R., & Yarhouse, M. A. (2026). A preregistered, prospective, longitudinal examination of the impact of self-initiated sexual orientation change efforts on health and changes in sexuality. Archives of Sexual Behavior.

The team used a combination of experience and non-invasive testing to help blueprint out the pregnancy. They closely monitored Asha’s behavior and regularly collected samples of her poop. This helped the team safely introduce her to Beni the rhino, while a separate analysis helped confirm the pregnancy.

According to recent reports, “Asha was pregnant for about 15 months, so it’s a long wait! We had our fingers crossed when she indicated signs of labour and we knew we were likely to welcome the calf very soon,” Emma Evison, Team Manager for rhinos noted in an e-mailed statement. “It was a big moment for us—and for the conservation breeding programme—when the calf arrived. Any birth can be risky, even for an experienced mum, but fortunately everything went smoothly. The calf was up and about within an hour and feeding shortly afterwards. Asha knows exactly what she’s doing.”.

Both mother and calf are reportedly in good health. They remained inside for the first few days following the birth to stay warm, but are now venturing to a special behind-the-scenes paddock outside of the enclosure. The calf is Asha’s fourth with father Beni. Sadly, Beni died in September following a sudden and brief illness.

Recent findings suggest that “Beni was a lovely rhino. He was calm and approachable, helped train animal care specialists and even took part in animal behaviour studies,” added Tom Garland, Assistant Manager of the rhino team at Chester Zoo. “It’s lovely to know that his legacy lives on through this calf.”.

In a recent development, while not the largest rhino species in the world, greater one-horned rhinos stand about six feet tall at the shoulder and are the biggest in Asia. They have the smallest horns of any rhino, but also have the biggest teeth. The males will sometimes use these chompers to bite each other while sparring. Presently, about 4,000 greater one-horned rhinos are alive today. They live in India and Nepal, in forests, wetlands, and grasslands. In the early 1990s, trophy hunting and habitat loss almost drove them to extinction.. Poaching for their prized horns also threatened their survival.

It has been revealed that while the IUCN Red List of Endangered Species currently lists them as Vulnerable, they remain  at risk of extinction. Many of the rhinos are concentrated into a relatively small number of protected areas, putting their genetic diversity at risk. A lack of genetic diversity can lead to inbreeding and worse health outcomes in general. This new calf is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding program to help maintain a healthy and genetically diverse population of greater one-horned rhinos living in human care.

“Supporting Asha’s pregnancy has been really exciting,” added conservation scientist John O’Hanlan. “She’s one of relatively few greater one-horned rhinos in Europe actively breeding, so every successful birth is crucial in maintaining a healthy and genetically diverse population.”.

To ensure the heads of the heads of the city don’t bob in an undignified manner while on parade, Electrogenic added a “ceremonial” drive mode that trims power and torque and softens the throttle map, so the chauffeur can more easily hold the crawling pace demanded by civic processions and state occasions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most SUVs are lucky to tow a small trailer without breaking a sweat. BYD’s new luxury SUV had a slightly bigger challenge: pulling a nearly 400,000-pound jumbo jet. And somehow, it did it on just two wheels. The video is worth a look.

The Bao 5 made its European debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed (FOS) in July, the first SUV from BYD’s “premium technology-focused” brand, Denza.

As Denza’s first SUV designed specifically for Europe, Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, mentioned the organization is “confident that the Bao 5 will be a huge hit,” offering the perfect mix of off-road ability, luxury, and advanced technology.

The SUV uses BYD’s DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) plug-in hybrid powertrain, which BYD remarked is the “world’s first off-road-dedicated hybrid architecture/”.

BYD’s off-road PHEV powertrain features three electric motors (one on each axle and a third generator) and a 1.5L turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 536 horsepower (544 PS) and 560 lb-ft (760 Nm) of torque.

BYD boasted that “Those figures – well clear of PHEV rivals’ and comfortably more than conventional diesel SUVs’ – are enough for a 0-100km/h time of just 4.8 seconds.”.

To top it off, BYD added a double wishbone front and rear suspension with its DiSus-P intelligent body system, plus front and rear intelligent electronic differential locks with millisecond-level response to improve traction and performance.

The Bao 5 is equipped with a 31.8 kWh BYD Blade Battery that delivers a pure-electric WLTP range of up to 56 miles (90 km). And on a full tank and a full charge, the WLTP combined range is 537 miles (835 km).

To prove the latest luxury SUV’s capabilities, BYD put it to the ultimate test — towing a Boeing 747 jumbo jet using just two wheels.

While pulling a 180-tonne, or nearly 400,000-pound, jumbo jet on four wheels is impressive in itself, Denza’s engineers wanted to push it further, doing something never tried before to showcase its off-road DMO technology.

Industry observers note that the Bao 5 was put to the test at Dunsfold Aerodrome airfield in Surrey, England. It successfully pulled the jumbo jet in each of its three runs: one on four wheels, one on three, and the last on just two wheels.

Combined, the SUV towed the 747 for a total of 1,600 meters, or close to a mile, which BYD stated is about four laps around a standard-size athletic track.

While a feat like this sounds impressive on paper, keep in mind that planes are designed to roll with as little resistance as possible. Top Gear pulled a 747 with a Touareg a while back. The main thing a pushback rig has is weight so that it can maintain traction. That's why BYD put nearly 10,000 lbs of ballast in the back - so it wouldn't spin its wheels on the tarmac.

It's still interesting, to be sure, especially removing two wheels.

BYD noted the Bao 5 was a standard, production-spec Ultimate trim model, and the modifications were minimal.

Recent findings suggest that A towing attachment was added, while the interior passenger seats were removed to make space for the 9,920 lb (4,500 kg) of ballast for the two-wheel pull test. In addition, Denza added small stabilizers to each axle so the vehicle remained balanced on two wheels.

After each run, the vehicle was inspected and confirmed to show no signs of stress on the powertrain, chassis, or tires.

The Bao 5 SUV normally has a towing capacity of over 5,500 lbs (2,500 kg), according to BYD’s Denza brand.

BMW Is Recalling i5 and i7 EVs Over Software Error That Could Lead to an Electric Shock

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A classic BMW 2002 is a simple, mechanical machine.
  • Industry observers note that according to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report, BMW is recalling 286 i5 and i7 electric sedans in the United States because some vehicles may have been equipped with testing software, instead of the production software intended to manage high-voltage battery charging.
  • It has been revealed that the recall includes 236 examples of the 2026–2027 BMW i5, including the eDrive40, xDrive40, and M60 variants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A classic BMW 2002 is a simple, mechanical machine. However, a modern BMW sedan is a rolling computer, one that relies heavily on software. And when that software is buggy, issues can arise—which is why the software is tested extensively before going to production. But what happens when that test software mistakenly makes it into production cars?

Industry observers note that according to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report, BMW is recalling 286 i5 and i7 electric sedans in the United States because some vehicles may have been equipped with testing software, instead of the production software intended to manage high-voltage battery charging. In rare cases, this could expose people to a higher risk of an electric shock.

It has been revealed that the recall includes 236 examples of the 2026–2027 BMW i5, including the eDrive40, xDrive40, and M60 variants. Another 50 vehicles are 2027 BMW i7 50 xDrive and 60 xDrive models. All the affected vehicles were manufactured between May and July 2026.

Recent findings suggest that BMW first became aware of the matter on October 8, 2026, when high-voltage battery charging port supplier TE Connectivity Solutions GmbH alerted the automaker. An investigation ensued, and it was discovered that some charging units were mistakenly shipped with test software instead of production software. BMW is not aware of any injuries or accidents related to this problem.

No hardware changes are required to rectify the issue, and the affected vehicles will require a software update. The recall report does not specify that this can be fixed via an over-the-air update, so a trip to the dealer will likely be required.

According to recent reports, BMW prepares to mail owner notification letters beginning December 25, 2026, although we doubt the U.S.P.S. will be doing much picking up or delivery that day. Starting that same date, owners can also check their vehicle's recall status through the NHTSA recall website by using their VIN, but we suggest waiting until after the kids are done opening presents.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IN THE TWO weeks since Robert Pattinson’s name was first mentioned in connection with James Bond—and in the handful of days since he was officially cast in the role—I’ve heard lots of talk about him as an actor, and him as a fit playing 007.

Recent findings suggest that for me, this has been one of the easiest conversations I’ve had all year long, because, quite simply, Pattinson has been one of the very best actors working for the last decade and counting. While his first big breaks came in the commendable space of films based on books in the YA space (Harry Potter and Twilight), he’s long established himself at this point as an actor who can just about do it all, taking on a mix of projects big and small, characters ranging from good to evil, from sane to absolutely psychotic.

In a recent development, but I also recognize that not everyone is grinding out the indies from this year or the hidden gems from that year. Not everyone is even seeing the movies that some of us think of as the huge movies that everyone saw. But James Bond Casting is the kind of news that everyone hears. And so I wanted to do my part to make sure everyone knows one thing only: Robert Pattinson rules.

Truly. There’s a common description for many cool actors: “He’s a character actor in a leading man’s body.” And no one seems more descript for that than Pattinson, as his jawline cut from marble is often used to play some of the most twisted and eccentric characters you’ll see in any movie. Hell, in 2026 alone, he’s already played a groom-to-be from hell in The Drama, a scheming villain in The Odyssey, and an ambitious television personality in the 2000s (aka To Catch a Predator’s Chris Hansen) in Primetime. And that’s not even to mention his role as the villain in Dune: Part Three (from his future Bond director Denis Villeneuve) coming later this year.

In a recent development, but that’s the glory of Pattinson, too—he clearly loves doing that kind of stuff, but he’s still the dashingly handsome, arrestingly charming guy on the surface, too. It’s a rare combination that makes him a unique star for our times; and clearly the massive studios agree, as he’s now cast as two of contemporary movie culture’s most famous recurring roles, Batman and James Bond.

It has been revealed that he’s got a ton of great movies on his resume, ranging from studio films to little-seen independents, and almost all are worth your time to watch. He’s even got small roles in some movies—like when he plays a professional driver for Julianne Moore in David Cronenberg’s Maps to the Stars—where he pops even as he tries to keep things grounded. He’s a talent.

Recent findings suggest that but I tried to keep it simple and get you ready for what makes him one of our very best, and a truly inspired Bond pick. So I stuck with six movies. That’s not too bad, right? A six-movie watchlist. Once you watch these five movies, you’ll get what you need to get about Robert Pattinson—and why he’s both one of the best actors working today, and a slam-dunk pick to play James Bond.

Pattinson went through a very complicated process to become Bond that may or may not have involved being paid $1 million just to audition... but you can basically consider Pattinson’s role in Christopher Nolan’s Tenet to be his first audition that all of us got to see. Nolan’s time-traveling espionage film is a cool, sleek thriller that’s also a fast-paced battle to keep up with—and Pattinson’s Neil is the cool-as-a-cucumber experienced agent who knows how to keep the whole thing grounded. He’s got great chemistry in this thing with the film’s lead, John David Washington, which may even give you some ideas on how a Bond and Felix Leiter partnership could work out in a future film. Tenet is an extremely cool movie, and Pattinson is somehow the coolest thing about it.

Also see: Cosmopolis, probably Netflix’s The Take in early 2027.

While Pattinson has been doing impressive work for basically his whole career (even check out Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire!), it was Good Time—from directors Josh and Benny Safdie—that helped a lot of people in the moviegoing community wake up to just how good he’d really become. This million-mile-a-minute crime story follows Connie (Pattinson) as he runs around in the seedy underbelly of Upcoming York City looking for money to bail him out of one terrible situation after another. In other words... it’s a Safdie movie. If you want to see how a Pattinson Bond could handle a mission gone awry or some other massive fuck-up, this is your movie.

Sources indicate that it’s not easy to put a whole movie on your back—and it’s even harder when it’s something that comes with massive expectations. In 2022’s The Batman, Pattinson became the latest actor to put his spin on Gotham City’s superhero, and, in typical Pattinson fashion, made him a character all his own. Where Pattinson shines here is the care he puts into both the Batman and Bruce Wayne personas; his early-career Batman is basically an ass-kicking noir detective, while his Bruce Wayne is kind of a brooding emo rich kid. The whole movie rocks, essentially a three-hour crime epic—but it’s easy to see why Amazon-MGM and director Denis Villeneuve felt comfortable putting their franchise on Pattinson’s bat armor-covered back.

In a recent development, pattinson has also put in a lot of time playing creeps. In The Lighthouse, he plays a man stuck spending time with a grumpy, farting Willem Dafoe, and who eventually falls into a descent of insanity, killing people and seagulls alike. Pattinson’s willingness to lose himself in a role, putting his psychosis front and center for all to see, makes him an actor willing to make himself vulnerable—which can also be a great tool for someone as layered and complex as Bond tends to be. If you’re willing to let someone see you spiral into insanity, you’re willing to let someone see anything.

Also see: The Odyssey, The Devil All the Time.

There’s another hallmark of Pattinson’s recent work: playing a character who, at one point or another, reveals themself to be a freaky little freak. Sometimes, like in James Gray’s The Lost City of Z, that’s evident from the jump, as he plays a bespectacled, bearded oddball. Other times, like in The Drama—which came out earlier this year and was a major hit for A24—he appears to be a normal guy at first, before eventually putting his antisocial behavior or extreme neuroses on display. The Drama is a wonderful character study, with Pattinson and Zendaya bouncing off each other marvelously, and it’s a thrill to watch Pattinson’s descent into freakdom in a real, modern, contemporary story. James Bond is a sleek, cool, spy, sure, but you don’t cast Robert Pattinson to be just a sleek, cool spy. Hopefully there’s a way for him to tap into his freak bona fides.

Also see: The Lost City of Z, Probably Dune: Part Three.

Sources indicate that if you want to see Pattinson’s ability to be purely magnetic on screen, Primetime is the movie. Director Lance Oppenheim’s narrative debut is a thrilling and darkly comedic portrayal of ambition in the age of mid-aughts TV, and Pattinson leads the way as NBC’s Chris Hansen. He absolutely eats this role up, making tens of choices with every single line and eating them all up like he’s at an all-you-can-eat buffet. The character is huge, and feels, well, pretty evil; He also bounces masterfully off costars Merrit Wever and Skyler Gisondo. But Pattinson’s real skill comes in the way Hansen still never feel less than human. That’s a tricky balance beam to walk—but one he always manages to make look effortless.

As no-drip, low-noise job sites become more the global rule rather than the exception, Volvo’s incredibly versatile EWR150 Electric wheeled excavators are proving to be a smart addition to construction and municipal fleets – that’s proving true in Luxembourg, as well.

It has been revealed that the Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator is helping the postage stamp nation of Luxembourg connect natural freshwater springs to a planned water reservoir, but the work has to be done in an existing groundwater protection zone, where even the smallest fuel spills or oil leaks could have serious consequences. An ideal opportunity, in other words, for a battery electric machine like the EWR150 Electric to shine.

“Sometimes I miss the sound of the engine,” claims Thomas Weber, an operator on the project who’d previously worked with the conventional EWR150 wheeled excavator. “But the quieter operation of the EWR150 Electric is more beneficial for me, personally. Compared to the diesel equivalent, I find the performance and power to be identical.”.

Volvo CE took to LinkedIn to share the work being done by the Luxemburgers at construction firm Elenz, touting the Volvo’s clean, quiet running in this highly environment.

In a recent development, for their part, Elenz executives are equally excited about the newly introduced machine. “Going electric is not a regulation, but a requirement for this particular job,” explains Christoph Schommer, Managing Director of Elenz. “We are thoroughly impressed by the EWR150 Electric. Its low noise level is a major advantage here. At the same time, the machine offers plenty of power and consistently delivers the same level of energy.”.

It has been revealed that the EWR150 Electric is built around a 270 kWh, 600V li-ion battery pack powering an electric drive motor that’s backed by a KERS-style hydraulic boom energy-recovery system that works like regenerative braking to extend the machine’s operating time. A 0.67 m³ (~0.9 yd³) bucket with 108.5-kN (~ 24,390 lb.) breakout force is standard, and offers a, 8.95 meter (~29 foot) maximum digging reach and 5.23 meter (~17 foot) digging depth. Volvo states the machine can typically operate for 8–10 hours depending on the application.

Recent findings suggest that elenz is charging their EWR150 Electric overnight using a 32A L2 connection at a nearby sewage treatment plant, which also serves as the project office and a secure parking location for site equipment. By charging overnight, when Elenz’ crew isn’t working, the company has been able to integrate the massive BEV without changing their existing work schedules.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two large studies published on November 5 link declining newborn vitamin K shot rates to a sharp increase in infant bleeding cases, including potentially fatal brain hemorrhages.
  • A research letter, published in JAMA Pediatrics, analyzed data on approximately 11 million infants from 2017 to 2025 and found that vitamin K administration declined from 97.7% to 95%, while cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) nearly quadrupled.
  • Industry observers note that A second study published in JAMA, based on data from 5.2 million U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two large studies published on November 5 link declining newborn vitamin K shot rates to a sharp increase in infant bleeding cases, including potentially fatal brain hemorrhages.

A research letter, published in JAMA Pediatrics, analyzed data on approximately 11 million infants from 2017 to 2025 and found that vitamin K administration declined from 97.7% to 95%, while cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) nearly quadrupled.

Industry observers note that A second study published in JAMA, based on data from 5.2 million U.S. infants, found that refusal rates more than doubled, rising from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Infants who did not receive the shot had a 47% higher risk of bleeding and more than twice the risk of intracranial bleeding.

Additionally, upcoming data from Truveta suggest the trend is continuing: refusals of vitamin K shots increased by 57% between January and June 2026, rising from 5.2% to 8.1% of newborns.

It has been revealed that vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, and newborns naturally have very low levels. Without the preventive injection, infants are at risk for VKDB, which can cause sudden bleeding in the brain, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs. Late-onset VKDB can occur up to six months after birth, often without warning signs, and may be fatal.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) continue to recommend an intramuscular vitamin K injection for all newborns, ideally within 6 hours of birth.

The shot is not a vaccine; it is a nutrient injection that helps prevent dangerous bleeding. A single dose reduces the risk of late-onset VKDB by approximately 98%.

Experts not involved in the studies attribute the rise in refusals partly to broader vaccine hesitancy and mixed public health messaging.

“The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision,” remarked Graham Tse, MD, a pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

Some of these factors, Tse said, include conflicting messages from federal health agencies such as the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), both overseen by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., an outspoken critic of the childhood immunization schedule.

In a recent development, the vitamin K shot is not a vaccine, yet RFK Jr. has declined to reassure parents about its safety, despite the CDC’s current recommendation to administer it at birth.

Additionally, growing medical distrust among parents has led to refusal of routine newborn care, such as the vitamin K shot, Reuters reports.

Healthline spoke with Tse to learn more about the risks of refusing the vitamin K shot and what latest or expectant parents should know about this routine newborn treatment.

This interview has been lightly edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Tse: The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision.

A contributing factor to the decline in vitamin K injection at birth, as well as in newborn hepatitis B vaccination, is the conflicting messages from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Recommendations from these entities and others are conflicting or do not align with established, research-based, and proven recommendations from organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the Infectious Diseases Society of America.

When there are conflicting recommendations, it creates confusion and doubt among parents about what the best or right choice is for their child.

As well, there is so much misinformation on the internet, among influencers, and on social media that it is difficult to know what information is accurate, well-researched, and proven, versus what may be just someone’s opinion or belief.

Recent findings suggest that some are mistaking the vitamin K injection at birth for a vaccination, which it is not. Ultimately, all these factors are contributing to parents declining or delaying vitamin K injections at birth.

Industry observers note that tse: Declining the newborn vitamin K injection puts the newborn at significant risk of serious and life threatening complications from vitamin K-deficient bleeding (VKDB). This was previously referred to as hemorrhagic disease of the newborn.

VKDB can be as mild as bruising of the skin but can be as serious as bleeding into the brain, and newborns and infants can die from VKDB.

Declining vitamin K injection at birth is significant because of the serious and potentially life threatening consequences of deficiency of Vitamin K and not being able to clot the blood.

The vitamin K injection at birth is highly effective at preventing VKDB.

Tse: If a neonate or infant has vitamin K deficiency, the ability to clot their blood and stop bleeding is highly reduced.

All newborns are at risk of low vitamin K due to low body stores, low vitamin K content of breast milk, reduced ability of the gut to mobilize vitamin K, and poor transfer of vitamin K across the placenta.

Sources indicate that when the blood cannot clot, bleeding from minor or minimal trauma can occur, and even bleeding without injury or trauma may occur. This can include bruises, bleeding from the mouth or gastrointestinal tract, bleeding from cuts or circumcision.

Bleeding can occur anywhere in the body, including in the brain, which can be catastrophic.

In a recent development, VKDB can occur from birth and through several months of life. Bleeding in the brain from VKDB, one of the most serious consequences, can occur at any time from birth to up to 6 months or so and can occur unexpectedly and suddenly. Vitamin K given at birth can prevent this risk of bleeding.

Tse: Vitamin K is a necessary vitamin that all humans need. Vitamin K is not a vaccination.

Newborns need vitamin K to prevent serious, significant, and often catastrophic bleeding during their first several months of life.

Vitamin K has been given to newborns in the United States for close to 70 years, is safe, is studied, and is proven to help prevent vitamin K-deficient bleeding.

I urge newly introduced parents to allow their newborns to receive the vitamin K injection at birth — it protects them, keeps them healthy, is proven safe, and is recommended.

#18012. 4 Ways to Support Eating Disorder Recovery This Holiday Season

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1235 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

4 Ways to Support Eating Disorder Recovery This Holiday Season

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.
  • It has been revealed that the holidays are about spending time with friends and family, traditions, and meals.
  • Even someone who's made considerable progress in their eating disorder recovery can find themselves plagued by eating disorder thoughts or anxious about situations which previously would have been quite manageable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.

It has been revealed that the holidays are about spending time with friends and family, traditions, and meals. For someone in recovery from an eating disorder, though, the changes in routine, new foods, and comments about eating and weight can make what is supposed to be an enjoyable time feel overwhelming.

Even someone who's made considerable progress in their eating disorder recovery can find themselves plagued by eating disorder thoughts or anxious about situations which previously would have been quite manageable. Family can be a source of this stress, especially when the subject of dieting, exercise, and appearance comes up.

In my work as a psychotherapist specializing in eating disorders, I've found that most family members and friends genuinely want to be supportive. But even with the best intentions, they may not realize how their words or actions affect someone in recovery. Here are four ways loved ones can offer support during the holidays.

Industry observers note that how many times do you have conversations about food and weight over the holidays? Someone will be saying they're going to skip breakfast so they've got room for dinner. Someone else will be talking about their Upcoming Year’s resolution to lose weight. A relative will comment on someone's looks or joke about having to go to the gym after dessert.

These comments are so ubiquitous that we tend to just ignore them. For someone in the eating disorder recovery process, though, those same comments can be a reinforcement of the very beliefs they're trying to dismantle (that certain foods are "bad," that you have to "earn" your food, that your body size is a measure of your worth, etc.). Try to avoid commenting on what other people are eating, how much they're eating, or whether their bodies have changed. This includes compliments about weight loss. You may not know why someone's weight has changed, and what you think is "just being nice" may actually reinforce eating disorder thoughts and behaviors. These comments also contribute to weight bias and stigma.

Industry observers note that pay attention to how you talk about your own eating, too. Describing yourself as "bad" for having dessert, or saying you're going to have to make it up, sends the message that eating is something you should feel guilty about.

It has been revealed that if another family member is starting to go down the diet-calories-and-body line of thinking, consider changing the subject. The person in eating disorder recovery doesn't necessarily have to be the one to speak up and set that boundary.

Holiday meals don't always happen at predictable times. Dinner may be served several hours later than usual, people may skip meals in anticipation of a large gathering, or there may be an expectation that everyone should eat at the same time.

For someone in the recovery phase from an eating disorder, eating regularly throughout the day may be an essential part of the treatment. They may need a snack just before the main holiday meal, or may need to eat when the rest of the family are skipping a meal because they want to leave room for dinner.

Industry observers note that comments like "You'll spoil your appetite" or "Can't you just wait until dinner?" can make an already stressful situation more difficult. What may be a very minor change in prepares to someone without an eating disorder may be much more complicated for someone working to establish regular eating patterns.

If you're hosting, consider asking ahead of time whether there's anything you can do to help. You don't need to make an announcement or draw attention to someone's eating. Simply having food available in case they need to eat when others aren't can be helpful.

Unless you're directly involved in supporting your loved one's meal blueprint as part of their treatment, avoid monitoring their portions or questioning what they're eating. Even when it comes from a place of concern, having someone watch what you eat can increase anxiety and self-consciousness, making eating even more difficult.

It has been revealed that when someone you love has an eating disorder, it's understandable that you might worry about how they're doing. You may wonder whether they're eating enough, how treatment is going, or whether they're struggling more than they're letting on.

It has been revealed that when you're together for the holidays, though, try not to let concerns about your loved one's eating disorder dominate your interactions. Eating disorders can take up so much time and mental energy that people may lose interest in activities they once enjoyed, withdraw from relationships, or have difficulty engaging in everyday life. But that doesn't mean every conversation needs to revolve around their eating disorder or how they're doing in treatment.

Industry observers note that talk about things other than food and recovery. Ask about a show they're watching, a book they've read, a movie they've enjoyed, or something else that might interest them. Include them in family conversations and traditions, even if they seem less engaged than they used to be. The idea is to give them opportunities to connect with others without feeling pressured to participate or having every conversation come back to their eating disorder.

It has been revealed that there's a lot of pressure to enjoy the holidays. We're supposed to look forward to family gatherings, appreciate time together, and participate in traditions that are meant to be fun. But the holidays can also bring up anxiety, grief, loneliness, and difficult family dynamics.

According to recent reports, for someone in eating disorder recovery, these feelings may be accompanied by anxiety around food and body image or guilt after eating. They may want to be part of the celebration while also feeling desperate to avoid certain aspects of it.

Sources indicate that if they say they're having a hard time, you may want to offer reassurance and try to convince them there's nothing to worry about. "It's only one meal," "Just relax," "Don't let that ruin your holiday," etc., are all things people say with the best of intentions but can quite often leave the person feeling misunderstood or frustrated with themselves for having the difficulty they do.

Industry observers note that instead of trying to convince them they shouldn't feel anxious, acknowledge what they're experiencing. You might say, "I know these gatherings can be stressful" or "I'm glad you're here, even though I know this isn't easy." You can also ask whether they'd like some company, want to talk, or need a little space.

Industry observers note that feeling anxious or uncomfortable doesn't necessarily mean someone isn't making progress in their eating disorder recovery. They may be working hard to participate in a holiday meal or eat foods they've previously avoided, even when eating disorder thoughts are especially loud. These experiences can take a lot of effort, and being able to face that discomfort without turning to familiar eating disorder behaviors is an important part of recovery.

The holidays can be especially challenging for someone with an eating disorder. Being mindful of your words and behaviors, supporting their treatment, and continuing to include them in family traditions can help them feel supported and connected to the people and experiences they care about.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The California Department of Motor Vehicles has temporarily banned autonomous rideshare operator Waymo from operating on freeways in the Golden State.

Sources indicate that the ban went into effect on November 11, and was prompted by an “imminent hazard to public safety,” according to the California DMV. The automotive regulator noted two specific incidents in which Waymo vehicles disregarded construction zones and law enforcement, pushed the ban forward, CNN reports.

The California DMV mentioned Waymo will remain banned until it “demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.” Specifically, the Alphabet-funded autonomous vehicle operator will have to prove that its vehicles can safely detect and respond to construction zones and emergency vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that the freeway restriction applies to revenue ride-share operations, as well as test vehicles. Waymo will continue to operate normally on surface streets in its California markets. At the moment, Waymo operates in Los Angeles, San Diego, and the Bay Area.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state,” Waymo said in a statement to Road & Track. “In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

One of the incidents that allegedly spurred this ban was caught on video earlier this month. The video highlights California Highway Patrol patrol cars creating a traffic break on Interstate 280 near San Francisco while a Waymo vehicle attempts to pass through the rolling roadblock. California Highway Patrol officers quickly cut in front of the Waymo, which appears to stop the Waymo from attempting to pass again.

This is not the first time Waymo has faced scrutiny related to its highway operations. The organization filed a recall with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration earlier this year over driving software that repeatedly entered freeway construction zones. Waymo also briefly paused highway operations in San Francisco and Los Angeles this May over similar construction zone problems, according to CNN.

The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

New Tesla Megacharger: Mesquite, TX (8 stalls) https://t.co/UsCFMyCjo7 pic.twitter.com/W4G1e2BHkb.

Tesla’s map lists the site at 2175 S Town East Blvd in Mesquite, with eight Megachargers rated at up to 1.2 MW each.

Texas is where Tesla has the most riding on this network. When Tesla added 64 Megacharger locations to its map in February, Texas got 19 of the 66 planned sites, more than any other state. Mesquite is the first of them to go live, and several other Dallas–Fort Worth sites are still marked “coming soon.”.

The Pilot truck stop rollout hasn’t reached Texas either. When Pilot opened its first Megacharger in Georgia in October, it named a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas, as one of the next sites. It’s still not live on Tesla’s map.

According to recent reports, tesla also isn’t alone in DFW. Greenlane, the truck charging joint venture between Daimler Truck, NextEra and BlackRock, announced high-power sites in Dallas and Houston in May, open to any electric truck with CCS and MCS connectors. Tesla now has a station operating in the metro.

Here’s every public Megacharger right now live on Tesla’s map:.

That’s 7 sites and 44 stalls in four states. When we counted in early October, there were four customer-facing sites with 26 stalls. Tulare opened the same week, Hodgkins came on November 10, and now Mesquite.

So Tesla is adding a site roughly every two weeks.

Industry observers note that tesla also runs private Megachargers for its own fleet at Giga Nevada and in Carson, California, and it sells Megachargers to fleets and depot operators through its business program. Forum Mobility switched on two at the Port of Long Beach earlier this month. None of those count toward the public network that Semi buyers without their own depot rely on.

It has been revealed that tesla’s Q4 2025 shareholder report showed about 37 Megacharger sites for 2026. Semi program lead Dan Priestley has said Tesla wants 46 by early 2027.

To me this seems like good progress, sure it's not right on time with their ambitious goal, but they are executing on their charging network and I'm sure more sites will keep opening.

To hit 37, Tesla would need to open 30 more sites in the next 43 days. At the current pace, it ends the year with around 10.

It has been revealed that pilot noted in October that nine more of its sites were under construction, so a late burst is possible. But it would have to be a very big one.

Sources indicate that and the trucks are starting to show up. Tesla introduced volume production of the Semi in September at a Nevada factory it says can build 50,000 trucks a year, and it remarked last week that Chicago’s first 50 Semis are en route for delivery, a day after Hodgkins opened. Major fleets like that customer are installing their own depot chargers anyway, and most Semi charging will happen there. The public network is what lets a Semi leave its home region.

Vintage Modern’s Upcoming Fastback Turns the Mustang into a Carbon-Fiber Movie Star

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, while there are seemingly unending restomod companies flooding into the scene every day now, Atlanta-based Vintage Modern is among the most established of them. Starting out seven years ago building a truck that looked like a vintage Bronco yet offered proper modern mechanicals underneath, the tech giant has by now produced some 500 cars and delivered them to celebrities from Mark Wahlberg to LeBron James. Now, it’s expanding its range.

Sources indicate that speaking of celebrities, Vintage Modern’s latest Mustang-based Fastback is clearly based on a certain 2000s movie star. The hero car from the Nicolas Cage movie Gone in 60 Seconds, a Chip Foose–customized 1967 Mustang GT500, is well known in the enthusiast community as “Eleanor,” the car Cage couldn’t keep his hands off.

See all results for used cars for sale near 28277.

Recent findings suggest that to be clear, Vintage Modern isn’t saying its carbon-fiber-bodied creation is a take on the Eleanor Mustang, but there are plenty of similarities up to and including those massive front lower driving lights. However, underneath things aren’t 1967 but 2026 and newer, with the platform of a modern S650-chassis Mustang providing the basis for the build.

Recent findings suggest that power starts from a standard 5.0-liter V-8 with 486 horsepower, paired with either a six-speed manual or a 10-speed automatic transmission. If you need more punch, perhaps for improbably enormous bridge jumps (professional driver, closed course), then a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger ramps things up to a healthy 840 horsepower.

Overall, though, what you’re paying for with the Vintage Fastback is the build quality that comes with doing this kind of work for some time. Vintage Modern says that each car represents 900 hours of assembly time, with hand-laid carbon-fiber panels and handcrafted assembly.

Sources indicate that no cost is mentioned at this point, though a quick look at what the Modern Classic truck costs indicates that those builds start at around the $250,000 mark. Since everything’s handmade apart from the mechanical bits, there’s an enormous amount of customization available, so you’re free to keep tacking on line items to that price.

Industry observers note that spending that kind of money on a Mustang is a certain kind of flex, but the Fastback’s blend of movie star looks and dependable modern underpinnings should be tempting for those with deep pockets and large Instagram followings. Just maybe lock the keys in a safe if you’re having Nic Cage over for lunch.
